title: Deshpande Hat-Trick Bowls Chandigarh Out for 78 as Mumbai Take Command at Wankhede
excerpt: Tushar Deshpande took 5 for 17, including a hat-trick in the 11th over, on day two of the Ranji Trophy season opener — becoming the sixth Mumbai bowler to take a Ranji hat-trick, and the first to do it at the Wankhede.
body:
• Tushar Deshpande took a hat-trick and finished Chandigarh's first innings with 5 for 17 as Mumbai bowled them out for 78, replying to Mumbai's 429.
  • The hat-trick — Arjun Azad, Shivam Bhambri and Dipender Kush in consecutive balls in the 11th over — made Deshpande the sixth Mumbai bowler with a Ranji hat-trick and the first to achieve one at the Wankhede Stadium.
  • Deshpande struck again after Mumbai enforced the follow-on, leaving Chandigarh 0 for 1 in their second innings at stumps on day two.
  • Across the round: Umesh Yadav took five wickets on his Punjab debut, Tripura's Sandip Sarkar took eight in a marathon spell against Hyderabad, and Ravindra Jadeja scored a century for Saurashtra.

Five wickets in a blur

The Ranji Trophy season is two days old and it already has its defining spell. Mumbai fast bowler Tushar Deshpande, playing his 50th first-class match, dismantled Chandigarh for 78 on Monday at the Wankhede Stadium, taking a hat-trick in the 11th over and finishing the innings with 5 for 17 from seven overs. Chandigarh had begun their reply to Mumbai's 429 in reasonable shape; within an hour, the innings was over.

Deshpande first bowled opener Arslan Khan in the seventh over. Then came the hat-trick over: Arjun Azad was caught by Sylvester D'Souza, Shivam Bhambri was bowled first ball, and Dipender Kush was caught by Yashasvi Jaiswal — also for a duck — leaving Chandigarh 25 for 4. Deshpande added Raj Bawa in the 13th over, Mohit Avasthi took 3 for 9 at the other end, and Chandigarh were all out for 78. After Mumbai enforced the follow-on, Deshpande struck once more in the only over before stumps, removing Vishu Kashyap for a duck to leave Chandigarh 0 for 1 and facing a mountain on day three.

A rare piece of Mumbai history

Deshpande is only the sixth Mumbai bowler to take a Ranji Trophy hat-trick, after Jehangir Khot, Umesh Kulkarni, Abdul Ismail, Royston Dias and Shardul Thakur — and, per reports, the first to do it at the Wankhede. It was his sixth first-class five-wicket haul, taking his career tally to 140 wickets. He had already contributed 44 off 47 balls in Mumbai's 429, an innings built on Siddhesh Lad's 86, Musheer Khan's 65 and half-centuries from Tanush Kotian and Mohit Avasthi, on a day when Jaiswal fell for a duck and Sarfaraz Khan made one.

Deshpande, 31, has played two T20Is for India but no Tests, and spells like this are his route back into contention. He was part of the India A squad that faced Australia A in September.

Around the grounds

Day two of the opening round delivered storylines across the country, per Cricbuzz's round-up: Umesh Yadav marked his Punjab debut — his first first-class outing in two years — with a five-wicket haul against Assam, for whom Denish Das and Sibsankar Roy scored centuries. Tripura offspinner Sandip Sarkar bowled 41.2 overs for eight wickets, yet Hyderabad still took a 160-run lead. Avesh Khan led Madhya Pradesh's rout of defending champions Jammu and Kashmir, bowled out for 120, and Ravindra Jadeja scored a century for Saurashtra against Chhattisgarh. Tamil Nadu, replying to Rajasthan's 363, reached 167 for 4 with neither Narayan Jagadeesan nor Pradosh Ranjan Paul converting their fifties. Full day-two coverage is at Wisden and Cricbuzz.
